title: RAG chunk record
description: One JSON object per line in rag_chunks.jsonl. Produced by scripts/build_rag_chunks.py from codebase/data/rag/*.json. Every value is copied or deterministically rendered from a source file; none is generated or inferred by a model.

id.description: Stable chunk id: <source-file-stem>::<pointer-slug>::<digest8>, where digest8 = first 8 hex of sha256('<source_file>#<source_pointer>'). Depends only on file name and JSON pointer, so it is identical across runs and machines and survives content edits.

source_file.description: Basename of the originating JSON file.

source_type.description: The originating file's own top-level `doc_type` value. Copied verbatim, not normalized into a controlled vocabulary.

title.description: The chunk's own heading, from the source unit's `title`/`milestone`/`event_type`. For timeline weeks it is composed as 'Tuần <n> (<range>)' from the source `week` and `range` fields.

section.description: Parent grouping: the file's `section.name` where present, or the parent document title for knowledge-base entries. Null where the source file declares no section (cohort3_evening_calendar.json).

content.description: Plain text, no markup. One source item per line, newline-separated. Object items are rendered by a fixed template per shape (command/description, level/name/threshold_xp, order/title/detail, title/detail/importance/reason) so no source field is dropped. This is the field to embed.

summary.description: EXTRACTIVE, 1-2 units max. Prose chunks: the first 1-2 sentences of `content`. List chunks: the first 2 lines joined with '; ', suffixed '; …' when more lines follow. Never model-generated, so it cannot introduce a claim absent from the source.

keywords.description: Union of the source unit's `tags`/`keywords` and the file-level `keywords`, in that order, casefold-deduplicated, first-spelling preserved. File-level terms are included so a chunk stays retrievable by document-wide vocabulary.

cohort.description: From `metadata.cohort`. Null for master_timeline.json, which states no cohort anywhere — deliberately not inferred from sibling files.

version.description: Version of THIS chunk schema and the pipeline that emitted the record. Not a version of the source document — no source file carries one. Bump when the record shape or rendering rules change.

status.description: Lifecycle. Grounded where the source states one: master_timeline `status` and knowledge-base week `status` map 'Đã xong'->completed, 'Hiện tại'->active, 'Upcoming'->upcoming. Every other chunk defaults to 'active' because no other source declares a lifecycle. Filter to active+upcoming for 'what is happening now' queries.

priority.description: Most specific source priority available (chunk > block/event > file `metadata.priority`); null when none is stated. CAUTION: each file uses its own scale — master_timeline uses 1-6 as week ordinals, other files use 1-2 as importance. Not globally comparable; safe to compare only within one source_file.

updated_at.description: Filesystem mtime of the source file, UTC, second precision. NOT an authored/publication date — no source file carries a timestamp. Use for recency tie-breaks only, and re-derive after any git operation that rewrites mtimes.

created_at.description: Same filesystem mtime as `updated_at`. The sources carry no creation date; the field is present for schema compatibility and must not be read as authorship time.

day.description: ISO date when the chunk pins to exactly one calendar day. Null otherwise — including the Demo Day chunks, which span three dates (see rag_ingestion_notes.md).

week.description: Program week 1-6, from the timeline `week` field or parsed from a 'Tuần <n>' heading. Null for chunks that are not week-scoped.

event_type.description: Calendar event class, only present in cohort3_evening_calendar.json.

source_path.description: Repo-relative path to the source file.

source_pointer.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the exact source node this chunk was built from. With source_path it reconstructs the origin byte-for-byte: `jq '<pointer>' <source_path>`.

language.description: The source file's declared `language`. All current sources are 'vi' (Vietnamese) — relevant when choosing a multilingual embedding model.

source_origin.description: Provenance of the source material as declared by the file: its `source_type` (e.g. 'image') or `metadata.source`. Records that a chunk ultimately derives from a transcribed calendar image rather than authored text.

hash.description: sha256 of NFC-normalized, whitespace-collapsed `content`. Drives exact-duplicate detection and lets ingestion skip unchanged chunks on re-runs. Changes if and only if the text changes.
